transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well... to be honest, I'm only here because my wife and my cardiologist insisted. Ever since my heart stopped a couple of years ago, I go out of my way not to think or talk about what happened or anything to do with doctors. I just... I really don't like bringing it up.
Since that heart-stopping event, do you ever have unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks of it, or feel very on edge when something reminds you of it?

Yes, quite often—even when I'm just sitting in the garden, I’ll suddenly picture myself back on the kitchen floor, hear my wife screaming, and my chest tightens like I'm dying all over again. I also feel constantly on edge, always checking my pulse and scanning for exits or phones in case it happens again.
Have these symptoms been going on for more than one month, and do you also avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of the heart-stopping event?

Yes, they've been going on for over two years now, ever since it happened. I definitely avoid things—I'll change the subject or leave the room if anyone brings up my health, and I even avoid walking past the hospital. I've also stopped volunteering at the senior center and seeing my friends because it all just feels like too much.
Since the event, do you ever feel numb or detached from other people, have trouble feeling positive emotions, or feel like the world or your body is unreal when reminded of it?
No, I wouldn't say I feel emotionally numb or like things are unreal in that way. I do feel very anxious and on edge most of the time, though, which is why I tend to keep to myself so much more now.
Do you ever have sudden nightmares or flashbacks of the heart-stopping event, or feel like it is happening again when you are reminded of it?

Yes, I get those flashbacks quite often, and they just come out of nowhere when I'm watching TV or sitting in the garden. I'll suddenly see myself back on the kitchen floor and hear my wife screaming my name. My chest tightens up so much that it truly feels like I'm about to die all over again in that moment.
Since the heart-stopping event, have you had any persistent guilt, blame, or a strongly negative view of yourself or the world because of what happened?

Yes, I constantly feel like my body is a ticking time bomb and that the world isn't safe anymore, like death could sneak up on me at any second. I also blame myself for the collapse, feeling like I brought it on by ignoring warning signs and not taking better care of my health over the years, even though the doctors said it was just an electrical issue.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder after a life-threatening cardiac arrest event: he has recurrent intrusive memories/flashbacks, marked avoidance of reminders and conversations about the event, persistent hypervigilance and exaggerated threat perception, negative beliefs and self-blame, symptoms lasting more than 2 years, and clear functional decline with social withdrawal and stopping volunteer activities.
